metadata.methods_description: Participants performed a semi-automated driving simulation task involving lane maintenance, following distance management, and collision avoidance with oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Multimodal physiological data were recorded including EEG, EOG, ECG, EDA, and gaze position tracking. The autonomous driving assistant could manage following distance alone or in combination with lane position maintenance, but required manual operator intervention for collision avoidance. Six experimental conditions were tested: practice baseline, manual driving, full autonomy with poor performance, full autonomy with good performance, speed-only autonomy with poor performance, and speed-only autonomy with good performance. State measures were derived from EEG, EOG, ECG, EDA, gaze position tracking, and subject vehicle control behaviors to develop psychophysiology-based metrics for monitoring trust in automation.
